spec.name: ESP32 DevKit V1 (ESP-WROOM-32)
spec.description: Dual-core 32-bit MCU with integrated Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n and Bluetooth Classic + BLE. 3.3 V logic, 30 usable GPIO, 12-bit ADC, LEDC PWM, capacitive touch. Powered over USB or VIN (5 V) with an on-board 3.3 V regulator.

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.signal: Strapping pin, on-board LED on most DevKits

pins.name: GPIO12
pins.signal: Strapping pin (MTDI) — drives flash voltage, avoid as an output at boot

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.signal: UART2 RX (PSRAM shares these on WROVER modules)

pins.name: GPIO34
pins.signal: ADC1_CH6 — INPUT ONLY, no internal pull-up

pins.name: GPIO35
pins.signal: ADC1_CH7 — INPUT ONLY, no internal pull-up

libraryRequirements.name: ESP32 Arduino core
libraryRequirements.purpose: Board support package for the ESP32

spec.name: Arduino Uno R3
spec.description: Arduino Uno R3 development board with ATmega328P, USB-B, barrel jack, header rows and on-board power circuitry.

spec.name: Arduino Nano
spec.description: ATmega328P in a DIP-30 breadboard-friendly form factor. Electrically equivalent to the Uno with 8 analog inputs (A0–A7) and a mini-B / micro-USB connector.

pins.name: A6
pins.signal: Analog only — cannot be used as digital

pins.name: A7
pins.signal: Analog only — cannot be used as digital

spec.name: Arduino Mega 2560
spec.description: ATmega2560 based board: 5 V logic, 54 digital I/O (15 PWM), 16 analog inputs (10-bit ADC), four hardware UARTs and 8 KB of SRAM. The board to reach for when a Uno runs out of pins — many-sensor builds, 3D printers, large relay/multiplexed designs. Same per-pin limits as the Uno: 40 mA absolute max, 20 mA recommended, ~200 mA total through the on-board regulator.

pins.name: D0
pins.signal: Serial RX — shared with the USB serial bridge

pins.name: D1
pins.signal: Serial TX — shared with the USB serial bridge

pins.name: D53
pins.signal: SPI SS — leave as OUTPUT even when unused, or SPI slips into slave mode

pins.name: 3V3
pins.signal: 50 mA max from the on-board regulator

pins.name: GND
pins.signal: Common ground — five physically separate pins, all the same net

pins.name: AREF
pins.signal: External analog reference for the ADC — only drive it after analogReference(EXTERNAL)

spec.name: SG90 micro servo
spec.description: 9 g hobby servo: 23 x 12.2 x 29 mm body with mounting tabs, output spline on top and a 3-wire lead. Position is commanded by a 50 Hz pulse between 0.5 and 2.5 ms.

spec.name: NEMA 17 bipolar stepper motor
spec.description: NEMA 17 frame: 42.3 mm square body, 47 mm long, 5 mm D-shaft, 31 mm bolt circle. Four leads for two coils, driven from a chopper driver.

spec.name: A4988 stepper driver breakout
spec.description: Microstepping chopper driver for bipolar steppers: STEP + DIR interface, 1/1 to 1/16 microstepping, motor supply 8–35 V, logic 3–5.5 V, up to 2 A per coil with a heat sink (≈1 A without). Requires a bulk capacitor across VMOT/GND and VREF trimming for coil current.

pins.name: RST
pins.signal: Reset (active low) — usually jumpered to SLP

pins.name: SLP
pins.signal: Sleep (active low) — usually jumpered to RST

spec.name: DHT22 (AM2302) temperature & humidity sensor
spec.description: Single-wire digital temperature (-40–80 °C, ±0.5 °C) and humidity (0–100 %RH, ±2 %) sensor. 0.5 Hz maximum sample rate, 3.3–6 V supply. Needs a 4.7–10 kΩ pull-up on DATA.

libraryRequirements.name: Adafruit Unified Sensor
libraryRequirements.purpose: Dependency of the DHT sensor library

spec.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor
spec.description: Ultrasonic ranging module with 2cm to 400cm non-contact measurement capability.

spec.name: HC-SR501 PIR Motion Sensor Module
spec.description: Pyroelectric infrared motion detection module with adjustable sensitivity and delay time.

spec.name: HX711 24-bit load-cell amplifier
spec.description: 24-bit ADC dedicated to strain-gauge bridges: connects a 4-wire load cell (E+/E-/A+/A-) to two ordinary GPIOs through a bit-banged clock/data protocol. Selectable gain 128/64 (channel A) or 32 (channel B), 10 or 80 samples per second. Needs a tare and a known-mass calibration factor in firmware.

pins.name: DT
pins.signal: Serial data out — goes LOW when a conversion is ready

pins.name: SCK
pins.signal: Serial clock in (also sets gain by pulse count)

pins.name: E+
pins.signal: Bridge excitation + (to the load cell red wire)

pins.name: E-
pins.signal: Bridge excitation - (to the load cell black wire)

pins.name: A+
pins.signal: Channel A signal + (load cell white/green wire)

pins.name: A-
pins.signal: Channel A signal - (load cell green/white wire)

libraryRequirements.name: HX711
libraryRequirements.purpose: Reading and scaling the 24-bit bridge value

spec.name: MQ-2 gas / smoke sensor module
spec.description: Heated tin-dioxide sensor for LPG, propane, hydrogen, methane and smoke. The module carries an on-board heater, a comparator with a digital output (DO) and an analog output (AO) for ppm estimation. 5 V supply, heater draws 150–800 mA and needs 24–48 h burn-in for stable readings.

pins.name: DO
pins.signal: Digital threshold alarm (active low on most modules)

spec.name: NTC thermistor temperature module (analog out)
spec.description: 10 kΩ NTC thermistor on a comparator board with a single amplified output. Read OUT with an ADC pin and convert with the beta/Steinhart-Hart equation — the module only scales the divider, it does not linearise. Output falls as temperature rises (NTC: resistance drops when hot).

spec.name: Tilt sensor module (SW-520D ball switch)
spec.description: Metal-ball tilt switch on a comparator board: OUT pulses LOW (on most boards) while the ball rolls and goes stable when the module settles past ~±10° from horizontal. Digital-only output — for a continuous angle use an accelerometer such as the MPU6050. Debounce: the ball chatters while moving.

pins.name: OUT
pins.signal: Tilt alarm — pulses while the ball rolls

spec.name: u-blox NEO-6M GPS module
spec.description: u-blox NEO-6 receiver on a breakout with antenna, backup battery holder and status LED. Streams NMEA 0183 sentences (GGA/RMC/VTG) over UART at 9600 baud; a TinyGPS-class parser assembles position, altitude, speed, course and UTC time. 2.5 m CEP accuracy outdoors, 50 channels, ~27 s typical cold start (1 s hot). Give it clear sky view — accuracy collapses indoors.

pins.name: TX
pins.signal: NMEA data out — wire to the MCU RX

pins.name: RX
pins.signal: Configuration commands in — wire from the MCU TX (optional if you only read)

pins.name: PPS
pins.signal: Pulse-per-second, accurate to ~ns — wire only when time-syncing, not needed for position

spec.name: DS3231 high-precision RTC module (ZS-042)
spec.description: Temperature-compensated real-time clock: ±2 ppm between 0-40 °C (about ±1 minute per year), seconds/minutes/hours/day/date/month/year with leap-year correction, on-chip aging trim and an integrated temperature sensor readable over I2C. The ZS-042 breakout adds a CR2032 backup holder so time survives power loss, plus SQW and 32K output pins. Careful on a shared bus: the DS3231 answers at 0x68 — the SAME address as an MPU6050. Move the IMU to 0x69 (AD0 high) or use one or the other.

pins.name: SQW
pins.signal: Programmable square wave 1 Hz-8 kHz (also a configurable alarm pin)

pins.name: 32K
pins.signal: 32.768 kHz clock output, enabled by register

libraryRequirements.name: RTClib
libraryRequirements.purpose: DS3231 register driver and DateTime helpers

spec.name: 5 mm LED
spec.description: Standard 5 mm through-hole LED. Forward voltage ~1.8–2.2 V (red/amber) or ~3.0–3.4 V (blue/white) at 20 mA. Always driven through a current-limiting series resistor: 220 Ω from a 5 V pin, 100–150 Ω from a 3.3 V pin.

pins.name: A
pins.signal: Anode — long leg, to the MCU pin through a resistor

spec.name: Active buzzer (5 V)
spec.description: Self-oscillating piezo buzzer: drive the + terminal HIGH/LOW for on/off — no PWM tone generation required. ~30 mA at 5 V, so it can be driven directly from a 5 V logic pin but should use a transistor on 3.3 V boards.

spec.name: WS2812B addressable LED strip (NeoPixel)
spec.description: Single-wire 800 kHz addressable RGB LEDs, 5 V supply, up to ~60 mA per LED at full white. Data in is a strict timing protocol; level shift from a 3.3 V MCU and inject power at both ends for long runs.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.signal: Data out to the next segment

spec.name: WS2812 8-LED ring (NeoPixel ring)
spec.description: Circular PCB carrying 8 addressable WS2812B LEDs chained on a single data line. Same electrical rules as a NeoPixel strip: 5 V supply, 800 kHz timing, one pin drives the whole ring, DOUT exists for chaining a second ring. Full-white draw is ~0.5 A (8 × 60 mA) — budget it on the 5 V rail, and add ~470 µF across the ring supply.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.signal: Data out to the next ring in the chain

spec.name: WS2812B 8x8 LED matrix (NeoPixel matrix, 64 pixels)
spec.description: 64 addressable WS2812B LEDs in an 8x8 grid on one data line — the same single-pin protocol as the strip and ring, scrolled into a matrix. One pin drives every pixel (index = row*8 + col with the common left-to-right, top-to-bottom wiring; cheap boards vary, so verify direction before fixing a layout). Full-white draw is ~3.8 A: budget a dedicated 5 V supply, inject power at the connector, and keep data runs short with a ~330-470 ohm series resistor and a ~1000 uF cap across the supply.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.signal: Data out to the next matrix in the chain

spec.name: 9 V alkaline battery (PP3)
spec.description: Convenient 9 V source for low-current projects. Internal resistance rises quickly: it can only supply a few hundred milliamps, so it is unsuitable for motor stall loads but fine for sensors and logic.

spec.name: LM7805 5 V linear regulator (TO-220)
spec.description: Classic positive linear regulator: 7–35 V in, 5 V out, up to 1.5 A with a heat sink. Needs ~2 V headroom and dissipates (Vin - 5) x I as heat, so it is inefficient for motor battery supplies. Add 0.33 µF on the input and 0.1 µF on the output.

spec.name: 1N4007 rectifier / flyback diode
spec.description: 1 A, 1000 V general-purpose rectifier diode. Across an inductive load (relay coil, raw DC motor) it clamps the back-EMF spike when the current is interrupted. Cathode (striped end) goes to the positive side of the load.

pins.name: A
pins.signal: Anode — to the low side of the load

pins.name: K
pins.signal: Cathode (striped) — to the high side of the load

spec.name: 1N4148 small-signal switching diode (DO-35)
spec.description: The fast small-signal diode: 100 V reverse, ~150 mA continuous forward, 0.6-0.7 V drop at tens of milliamps and a ~4 ns recovery that makes it the standard clamp for logic-level switching, steering/OR-ing inputs and small relay/buzzer coils. For anything above ~100 mA continuous use a 1N4007; for low-drop rectification use a Schottky.

pins.name: A
pins.signal: Anode — toward the more positive point when forward-biased

spec.name: 1N5819 Schottky diode (40 V, 1 A)
spec.description: Schottky barrier rectifier: ~0.45 V typical forward drop at 1 A (0.6 V max) against the ~0.9 V of a silicon diode, and essentially zero recovery time. The choice where every hundred millivolts is heat or runtime: reverse-polarity protection in series with a supply rail, low-voltage rectification, flyback on bigger coils where a hot diode wastes your budget. 40 V reverse limit — not for mains-side work.

pins.name: A
pins.signal: Anode (black bar end is the cathode)

pins.name: K
pins.signal: Cathode — to the more positive point in a protection diode

spec.name: 220 Ω resistor (1/4 W)
spec.description: 220 Ω, ±5 %, 1/4 W through-hole resistor. The standard LED current limiter from a 5 V logic pin (≈13 mA at a 2.1 V LED).

spec.name: 100 nF ceramic decoupling capacitor
spec.description: 100 nF (0.1 µF) 50 V ceramic capacitor placed between VCC and GND of every IC to suppress high-frequency supply noise.

spec.name: 6 mm tactile pushbutton
spec.description: Momentary 4-leg tactile switch. Legs on the same side are internally connected, so use one leg per side. Wire between a GPIO and GND with the internal pull-up enabled (reads LOW when pressed), or between GPIO and VCC with a pull-down.

spec.name: 4x4 membrane keypad
spec.description: 16-key membrane matrix keypad (1-9, 0, *, #, A-D). Eight pins, not sixteen: the MCU drives the four row lines (R1-R4) low one at a time and reads the four column lines (C1-C4) through its internal pull-ups. A pressed key shorts one row to one column, so the firmware resolves the key from the (row, column) pair.

spec.name: 10 kΩ rotary potentiometer
spec.description: Three-terminal 10 kΩ linear-taper rotary potentiometer. Connect the two outer terminals to VCC and GND and read the wiper with an ADC pin for an analog input.

pins.name: WIPER
pins.signal: Center tap to an ADC pin

spec.name: 10 kΩ slide potentiometer (fader)
spec.description: Linear-taper 10 kΩ slide potentiometer (45 mm travel fader). Electrically identical to a rotary pot: the two ends go to VCC/GND and the wiper to an ADC pin, with position proportional to travel. Choose it over a rotary pot when the panel layout wants a visible, directly-labelled position — mixers, light dimmers, setpoint sliders.

pins.name: A
pins.signal: One end of the track to VCC

pins.name: B
pins.signal: Other end of the track to GND

spec.name: 8-way DIP switch (SPST)
spec.description: Row of eight independent slide switches in a standard 0.1" DIP package — the classic way to give a device a hard-wired address, mode or configuration word that survives power cycles. Each pole is a separate pair of pins (nA/nB); wire one side to the MCU pin and the other to GND, and enable the internal pull-up so OFF reads HIGH and ON reads LOW.

pins.name: 1B
pins.signal: Switch 1 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 2B
pins.signal: Switch 2 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 3B
pins.signal: Switch 3 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 4B
pins.signal: Switch 4 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 5B
pins.signal: Switch 5 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 6B
pins.signal: Switch 6 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 7B
pins.signal: Switch 7 pole, side B (wire to GND)

pins.name: 8B
pins.signal: Switch 8 pole, side B (wire to GND)

spec.name: KY-040 Rotary Encoder Module
spec.description: Incremental rotary encoder with built-in momentary push button switch and pull-up resistors.

spec.name: SPDT slide / toggle switch
spec.description: Single-pole double-throw mechanical switch: the common terminal is connected to exactly one of the two throws at all times. Use it as a hard power switch or as a latching logic input (common to the GPIO, one throw to GND, internal pull-up enabled).

spec.name: 2-axis analog thumb joystick module
spec.description: PS2-style thumb joystick: two 10 kOhm potentiometers on X and Y plus a momentary push switch under the stick. Each axis reads roughly mid-scale at rest (about 512 on a 10-bit ADC) and needs a dead-band in firmware because the spring return is not exact.

pins.name: VCC
pins.signal: Supply — sets the ADC full-scale reference for both axes

pins.name: SW
pins.signal: Push switch, active LOW, needs an internal pull-up

spec.name: 830-point solderless breadboard
spec.description: Full-size solderless breadboard: 63 columns of 5-point tie rows split by a center DIP channel, plus two power rails per side. This is the wiring medium, not an electrical component — it does not appear in the connection graph.

spec.name: 1602 LCD with I2C backpack (PCF8574)
spec.description: 16x2 character LCD on a PCF8574 I2C backpack. Only four wires are needed (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL). Default address 0x27 (some backpacks use 0x3F), 5 V supply with a contrast trimmer and backlight jumper.

libraryRequirements.name: LiquidCrystal I2C
libraryRequirements.purpose: PCF8574 backpack driver for HD44780 LCDs

spec.name: 0.96" I2C OLED Display (SSD1306)
spec.description: 128x64 pixel monochrome OLED display module communicating over I2C interface.

spec.name: 2004 LCD with I2C backpack (PCF8574)
spec.description: 20x4 character LCD on a PCF8574 I2C backpack — the 16x2 layout with two more lines for menus and telemetry. Four wires only (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL). Default address 0x27 (some backpacks use 0x3F), 5 V supply with contrast trimmer and backlight jumper.

libraryRequirements.name: LiquidCrystal I2C
libraryRequirements.purpose: PCF8574 backpack driver for HD44780 LCDs

spec.name: 1-digit 7-segment display (common cathode, 5161AS)
spec.description: Single-digit 10-pin common-cathode 7-segment LED display (0.36", 5161AS-style). Each segment is an independent LED: drive segments HIGH through 220-330 Ω resistors while holding the common cathode at GND. Multiplex several digits by sharing segment lines and switching each COM in turn.

pins.name: COM
pins.signal: Common cathode (the package exposes two COM pins on one internal net)

spec.name: 10-segment LED bar graph (JL-B10D style)
spec.description: Ten independent LEDs in a bar package, 20 pins: anodes A1-A10 on one side, cathodes C1-C10 on the other. Each segment needs its own series resistor and its own pin (or a charlieplexed/multiplexed arrangement). The classic VU meter / level indicator: light n segments for a 0-10 reading.

spec.name: 2.8" ILI9341 SPI TFT display (240x320, ILI9341)
spec.description: 2.4-3.2" colour TFT panels share one driver: an ILI9341 controller over SPI with a 240x320 RGB-565 framebuffer. Wired 4-wire SPI plus D/C (command/data select), CS and RESET; the LED pin is the backlight anode, fed from 3.3 V or a GPIO-controlled transistor — the module carries the current-limiting hardware. Check the silk: many boards label MOSI as SDI and MISO as SDO.

pins.name: DC
pins.signal: Data/command select: LOW = command, HIGH = data

pins.name: SDI
pins.signal: SPI MOSI — data from MCU to the panel

pins.name: LED
pins.signal: Backlight anode — module carries the driver; feed from 3.3 V or a switching transistor

pins.name: SDO
pins.signal: SPI MISO — only needed when reading from the controller (most sketch loops never do)

spec.name: 2N2222 / PN2222 NPN transistor (TO-92)
spec.description: The default small-power NPN. VCEO 40 V, 600 mA continuous collector current (1 A peak), hFE 100-300. As a low-side switch from a GPIO: base resistor = (Voh - 0.7 V) / (Ic / 10) — roughly 1 kohm for 100 mA from a 5 V pin, 470 ohms from 3.3 V. VCEsat is ~0.3 V at 150 mA, so it dissipates (0.3 V x Ic) — fine to ~200 mA in free air.

pins.name: B
pins.signal: Base — drive through a series resistor (rule of thumb: Ic/10 for hard saturation)

pins.name: C
pins.signal: Collector — to the load; the load returns to the supply

spec.name: 2N7000 N-channel MOSFET (TO-92)
spec.description: Small logic-friendly NMOS: rated 200 mA continuous, RDS(on) roughly 2-5 ohm with a 4.5 V gate. Good for LEDs, small relays and buzzers from a 5 V GPIO through a ~100 ohm gate resistor. At 3.3 V it is already marginal — check your load current; this is NOT the part for amps.

pins.name: G
pins.signal: Gate — voltage driven, no DC gate current; a ~100 ohm series resistor damps ringing

pins.name: D
pins.signal: Drain — to the load; the load returns to the supply

spec.name: IRF540N N-channel power MOSFET (TO-220)
spec.description: Classic power NMOS: 100 V, 33 A package rating, RDS(on) 44 mohm — but RDS(on) is specified at VGS = 10 V. It is NOT a logic-level FET: from a 3.3 V or 5 V GPIO it only half-enhances, sags under load and heats. Drive the gate with 10-12 V (or through a BJT/driver stage), or pick a logic-level part for direct GPIO drive. Always a low-side switch: source to GND, load between supply and drain.

pins.name: G
pins.signal: Gate — needs a real 10 V drive for the rated RDS(on); a GPIO alone will cook it under load

pins.name: D
pins.signal: Drain — to the load (motor +, heater, LED rail)

spec.name: PC817 optocoupler (phototransistor output)
spec.description: Single-channel optocoupler: an infrared LED facing a phototransistor in a 4-pin DIP, 5 kV input-to-output isolation. Drive the LED side from a GPIO through a ~330 ohm resistor (IF ~10 mA, VF 1.2 V); the collector/emitter side switches up to 80 V at ~50 mA. CTR (current transfer ratio) 50-600 % by rank — budget the output side at 2-5x the input current. The standard way to isolate a mains-side triac/relay stage or two hostile voltage domains from an MCU.

pins.name: ANODE
pins.signal: LED anode — from the GPIO THROUGH a series resistor (330 ohm at 5 V)

pins.name: CATHODE
pins.signal: LED cathode — to the driving MCU's GND

pins.name: COLLECTOR
pins.signal: Phototransistor collector — to the isolated side's pull-up/load

pins.name: EMITTER
pins.signal: Phototransistor emitter — to the isolated side's ground
